solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Problems exist over European exchange programme

indicators.note: turning something over flips it, so the words before are read from the end back to the start

parts.note: arithmetic problems set in school are sums
to exist is simply to be: they are

explanation.surface: Someone complains that difficulties surround a European student exchange scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: SUMS plus ARE, read from the end, gives ERASMUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus is the EU scheme that lets university students study for a spell in another European country.

clue.text: Extra for packet? More than enough soup without seconds

parts.note: an excess is more than is needed

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the soup sits around the next letter

parts.note: potage is a thick soup
s is the standard abbreviation for seconds

explanation.surface: A diner gets far too much soup and no second helpings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is the old sense of outside, not lacking. The question mark flags that the definition is a description rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Excess postage is the surcharge the post office levies when a parcel carries too few stamps for its weight.

clue.text: Man in suit failing to start Yankee's guaranteed payment

indicators.note: each word that fails to start loses its opening letter

parts.note: taken as written, then headless
taken as written, then headless
taken as written, then headless
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man in a suit fails to begin paying out an American's guaranteed income.
explanation.walkthrough: The deletion applies to all three words, not only to suit: (m)AN (i)N (s)UIT plus Y.
explanation.definitionFit: An annuity is a fixed sum paid every year, typically bought as a secure pension income.

clue.text: Principal Zulu city

parts.note: principal means chief or main
Zulu is Z in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: It names the chief city of the Zulu people.
explanation.definitionFit: Mainz is a German city on the Rhine, birthplace of Gutenberg's printing press.

clue.text: Dingy loos set up in Spitzbergen

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised upwards, so the letters run bottom to top

parts.note: dingy and drab both mean dull and dreary
lav is British slang for a lavatory or loo

explanation.surface: Grim toilets have been installed in an Arctic outpost.
explanation.walkthrough: Spitzbergen is the largest island of the group, so it stands for the archipelago as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Svalbard is the Norwegian Arctic archipelago whose main island is Spitsbergen; older usage gave the whole group that name.

clue.text: One holding a person's hat by peak

parts.note: a cap is a kind of hat
a tor is a rocky hill or peak, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Someone grabs another person's hat by its peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peak' looks like the brim of the cap, but it is a hilltop.
explanation.definitionFit: A captor is whoever has taken someone prisoner and keeps them confined.

clue.text: Look up in native American language

indicators.note: one item goes in another, sitting inside its letters

parts.note: the Cree are a First Nations people of Canada

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are written from the bottom

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look

explanation.surface: Someone looks something up in an indigenous American language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Native American language' wants to be the definition; native American is only the container, and language alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A creole is a fully fledged mother tongue that grew from a pidgin mixing two or more languages.

clue.text: Fighting spirit of dog can upset it over years

parts.note: a pug is a small breed of dog

indicators.note: upsetting things knocks them out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
y is the abbreviation for year or years

explanation.surface: A feisty dog's aggression can upset things over the years.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places the earlier pieces above Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Pugnacity is an eagerness to quarrel or fight, from the Latin pugnare, to fight.

clue.text: Wealthy work fast after university

indicators.note: after places the word for fasting second, following the university letter

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
U is the abbreviation for university
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A rich graduate works quickly once out of university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like an adverb for quick work; it is a period of fasting, placed after U.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent describes great riches or lavish luxury, as in an opulent palace.

clue.text: Is girl able to take out competitor?

parts.note: being able means you can
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
to take someone out romantically is to date them

explanation.surface: It asks whether a young woman is allowed to go out with a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: The question turns the order round: 'Is girl able' becomes 'Can Di?', so the able word comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate is someone standing in an election or contest, a contender for the prize.

clue.text: Complain doctor's consuming alcohol

indicators.note: something consuming another swallows it up, so it is placed inside

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
rum is an alcoholic spirit

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that the doctor is drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, grump means to grumble or sulk in a bad-tempered way.

clue.text: Mum or dad morally correct raising Henry with qualifications

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising the henry symbol lifts it higher up its word, ahead of the two letters above it

parts.note: either is a parent
ethical means morally right; the henry is the unit of inductance, symbol H

explanation.surface: An upright parent brings up a son called Henry, who has qualifications.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raising Henry' sounds like bringing up a child; it means the H in ETHICAL climbs two places, giving HETICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A parenthetical remark is an aside inserted to qualify or hedge the main statement.

clue.text: Fraud succeeded with one pair of unknowns

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees
w is the abbreviation for with
the Roman numeral for one
z is an algebraic unknown, so a pair is two of them

explanation.surface: A con artist got away with it, helped by two mystery partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Swizz is British slang for a swindle or a disappointing cheat.

clue.text: A large youth taking pint round for singer

indicators.note: one item placed round others encloses them

parts.note: a pint is a glass of beer
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large
a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: A big young man brings a round of pints to a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A balladeer is a performer of ballads, a folk or popular vocalist.

clue.text: Your associate has perhaps initially put back bract

indicators.note: putting things back sends them the opposite way, read from the end

parts.note: yr is the written abbreviation for your
an ally is a partner or associate

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the words just before it

parts.note: first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone's partner has perhaps first put something back.
explanation.walkthrough: YR ALLY HP read backwards gives PHYLLARY, an obscure botanical word best reached from the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A phyllary is one of the small leaf-like bracts that ring a daisy or thistle flower head.

clue.text: One keeping books in balance fled having concealed one

parts.note: Libra is the zodiac sign of the scales or balance

indicators.note: a thing that has concealed another hides it within

parts.note: fled means ran away
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper who balanced the accounts ran off hiding a stash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping books in balance' reads as accountancy, but the definition stops at books and balance is the star sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A librarian looks after a library's collection of volumes and lends them out.

clue.text: What to get after nine assembly toys for young one?

parts.note: a kit is a set of parts for building a model
counting on, ten comes after nine

explanation.surface: It asks what to buy after nine o'clock in the way of construction toys for a child.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the playful phrasing; the pieces are written in the reverse of their clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitten is a young cat, so it is a young one of the feline kind.

clue.text: Key runs under professional test champion

indicators.note: in a down entry, going under puts these letters below the ones that follow

parts.note: pro is short for professional
the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for British vehicles
E is a musical key
r is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A key player scores runs below a professional Test match champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Test champion' suggests cricket's Test matches, but test is the car check and champion is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A promoter supports and advocates a cause, just as a champion of it does.

clue.text: Dilapidated horse-drawn carriage carrying two bishops

indicators.note: a vehicle carrying passengers holds them inside

parts.note: a shay is a light horse-drawn carriage, also called a chaise
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, twice

explanation.surface: A rundown old carriage gives two bishops a ride.
explanation.definitionFit: Shabby means worn out and in poor repair, synonymous with run-down.

clue.text: Excuse a page on science

parts.note: taken as written
p is the abbreviation for page
an ology is a branch of science, from the suffix -ology

explanation.surface: A single page of science serves as somebody's alibi.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places A and P above OLOGY.
explanation.definitionFit: An apology can be an excuse, as in a poor apology for something, or a justification.

clue.text: Crustacean caught with light line by angler, perhaps

parts.note: c is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a ray is a beam or line of light
the angler is a fish, so it is an example of one

explanation.surface: A shellfish is landed on a light fishing line by someone angling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angler' looks like the person fishing; it is the anglerfish, and 'line' belongs with light.
explanation.definitionFit: A crayfish is a freshwater animal like a small lobster, a member of the crustaceans.

clue.text: Sloth in tree mostly climbing with another likewise

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means read from the bottom upward
mostly means all but a little, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: likewise says the next piece gets the same upward treatment

parts.note: the ai is the three-toed sloth, so another one

explanation.surface: A sloth climbs up a tree, along with a second sloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sloth' here is laziness, not the animal; 'another' quietly switches to the animal, since the ai is a sloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth as a deadly sin is idleness, and inertia is a sluggish disinclination to act.

clue.text: Small hint? Absolutely

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for small
to imply is to hint at something

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a tiny clue will do, and gets an emphatic yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Simply can mean utterly or completely, as in simply wonderful.

clue.text: Feature of Berg's music composed almost in A

indicators.note: something composed is put together anew, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A piece by the composer Berg was written nearly in the key of A.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' looks like a deletion signal but is plain fodder; Alban Berg was a Viennese composer of the Second Viennese School.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonalism is music without a home key, a hallmark of Berg's work alongside Schoenberg's.

clue.text: Be anxious having wife in residence

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside its letters

parts.note: a seat is a country residence, as in a family seat
w is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A man worries about having his wife living at home.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweat over something is to worry about it nervously, an informal idiom.

clue.text: Be mean with male interrupting dance

indicators.note: something interrupting breaks into the middle of another

parts.note: to skip is to move along with little dancing hops
m is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A nasty man barges in on someone's dance.
explanation.definitionFit: To skimp is to be stingy, spending or providing less than is needed.

clue.text: Mushroom used in kitchen Okinawa-style

indicators.note: what is used in a phrase is found inside its run of letters

parts.note: end of the first word, start of the second

explanation.surface: A mushroom is cooked in an Okinawan kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Okinawa-style' is surface colour; the hyphenated suffix plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: Enoki are thin, long-stemmed white fungi much used in Japanese cooking.

clue.text: Picture accepting a temperature disturbance for the country?

indicators.note: a thing accepting others takes them in, holding them within

parts.note: pic is short for picture
taken as written
t is the abbreviation for temperature
a riot is a violent public disturbance

explanation.surface: A news photo shows a riot breaking out as tempers rise across the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as loose: being for one's country, as opposed to against it.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriotic person loves and supports their nation, so they are on its side.

clue.text: Day in NY? Yes, fantastic city

indicators.note: fantastic means wildly fanciful, so these letters go into a strange new order

parts.note: d is the abbreviation for day
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tourist enthuses about a day in New York as fantastic.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface praises one city, New York, while the answer is another.
explanation.definitionFit: Sydney is Australia's largest city, home to the famous Opera House.

clue.text: Painter of heavenly figure

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Italian Renaissance artist
second meaning: one of the archangels

explanation.surface: It describes an artist who painted angels.
explanation.definitionFit: Raphael was the High Renaissance master of Urbino, and he shares his name with the archangel of the Book of Tobit.
